criteria: A public tagged source release contains the graph specification, JSON schemas, TypeScript interfaces, migration guidance, and worked examples. Public automated build checks pass for incident identity, required claim references, review metadata, relationship types, and reproducible generation against
A public dataset release contains at least 10 independently reviewed canonical incidents, with source references and review records.
milestones.name: Specification and first reviewed cases (months 1-2)

criteria: The public corpus contains at least 30 independently reviewed canonical incidents, cumulatively, with a published selection rationale and coverage-gap register.
A public reviewer-agreement report includes the measurement method, original assessments, reconciliations, and unresolved findings for the released corpus.
At least 30 control assessments are published with enforcement location, assumptions, failure mechanism, and evidence status.
A public CLI release includes executable analysis examples, OAK mappings, and a field-level STIX 2.1 compatibility note; its documented examples pass public automated build checks.
At least one external technical review report is published, covering incident deduplication, claim provenance, review completeness, and catalog validation.
milestones.name: Reviewed corpus, controls and tools (months 3-4)

criteria: A public reference viewer exposes incidents, relationships, control assessments, and supporting references from a tagged dataset release.
Public documentation describes installation, queries, contribution review, corrections, and license boundaries.
Every finding in the external technical review has a public disposition linked to a fix or documented rationale.
milestones.name: Reference viewer and handoff (months 5-6)

criteria: At least six independent external organizations publish dated evidence of using the map in an actual audit (that cost more than $30,000), wallet-security review  (that cost more than $30,000), or incident investigation  (of losses exceeding $200,000), identifying the dataset version and resulting work product.

At least three adopting organizations publish comparative evaluations, collectively covering wallet development, auditing, and incident response, with task descriptions, completion time, factual errors, missing evidence, and feedback.
At least two external audit work products publicly identify incident mappings or control assessments used in their analysis, with confirmation from the auditing organization.

A public adoption register links each counted organization to evidence on its own website or repository. It counts each organization once and excludes recipient affiliates, project staff, duplicate identities, demonstrations, automated accounts, and paid endorsements.
milestones.name: External use and evaluation (months 5-6)

sections.commitments:
- Tooling will use Apache-2.0. Project-owned database material will use CC BY-SA 4.0.
  Upstream terms and exclusions will be documented separately.
- Each canonical case will receive independent assessments from at least two external
  reviewers. Public records will retain original assessments, reconciliation decisions,
  and unresolved disagreements.
- The six-month targets are at least 30 reviewed incidents, 30 control assessments, six
  external adopting organizations, three comparative evaluations, and two external audit
  work products using the map.
- Henri Binsztok, through OKcontract Labs, will maintain releases and corrections for at
  least 12 months after the final milestone, with at least two maintainer-days per month
  funded from OKcontract Labs’ operating budget.
  The dataset supports the team’s automated audit work.
  Further corpus expansion will require sponsorship or new funding.
sections.in_scope:
1. Publish the graph specification: node and relationship semantics, incident surface
   roles, confidence levels, and primary-cause assessment rules.
   Include JSON schemas, TypeScript interfaces, migration guidance, and examples.
   Distinguish architectural relationships, observed incident relationships, and analyst
   hypotheses.
2. Strengthen provenance and incident identity.
   Attach references and review rationale to individual surface, relationship, and cause
   assertions. Record reviewer identities, dates, disagreements, and corrections.
   Normalize chain identifiers and support multiple transactions per incident.
   Separate source observations from canonical incidents to prevent duplicate incident
   counts and loss totals.
3. Publish a reviewed Ethereum L1 and L2 corpus spanning contract exploitation, signing
   deception, supply-chain compromise, governance, custody, bridges, and delegated
   authorization. Publish selection criteria and coverage gaps.
   Preserve unknown and disputed findings.
4. Assess defensive controls, including transaction verification, restricted delegation,
   release integrity, independent approval channels, and upgrade restrictions.
   Record enforcement location, assumptions, and whether each control prevents, detects,
   or limits the failure mechanism.
   Separate demonstrated protection from hypothetical applicability.
5. Release downloadable datasets, a query CLI, executable examples, and a small
   reference viewer. Publish mappings to [OAK identifiers](https://onchainattack.org/)
   and a field-level
   [STIX 2.1](https://docs.oasis-open.org/cti/stix/v2.1/os/stix-v2.1-os.html)
   compatibility note, including unmapped fields.
   Link available upstream exploit reproductions.
   Include machine-readable query outputs for defensive AI-agent workflows.
6. Recruit external users, support use in their work, and compare source-only and
   graph-assisted workflows.
   The grant covers onboarding, workflow support, evaluation design, and public evidence
   collection. Publish completion time, factual errors, missing evidence, and feedback,
   including neutral or adverse results.

The planning budget is $42,000 for 7 person-months at $6,000, $6,000 for independent
incident review and technical verification, and $2,000 for hosting and releases.
Milestone allocations are: specification, $9,000 labor, $2,000 review, $1,000
operations; corpus and tools, $9,000 labor, $3,000 review; viewer and handoff, $8,000
labor, $1,000 operations; adoption, $16,000 labor and $1,000 evidence verification.
These are planning allowances.
sections.out_scope:
Exhaustive incident coverage, live monitoring, emergency response, newly developed
exploit reproductions, and standalone commercial protocol audits are excluded.
Historical frequency and recorded losses will not be presented as calibrated
probabilities of future compromise.
Confidential incident material and upstream content without redistribution permission
are excluded from public downloads.

sections.why:
Ethereum applications depend on interacting technical and operational systems.
A security failure can begin in a software dependency or operator session, alter
transaction construction, pass through legitimate signing, and reach onchain execution.
Understanding those relationships is necessary to design effective protections.

Historical incident reports contain valuable evidence, but comparing them requires
repeated interpretation of terminology, system boundaries, causes, and consequences.
Onchain Risk Map will share that work through a maintained reference model and
reproducible dataset.
Auditors, wallet developers, projects, and incident responders will be able to find
comparable incidents, inspect affected trust boundaries, and assess proposed defenses.
The scope addresses wallet experience, smart contract security, infrastructure, and
incident response in the Ethereum Foundation’s linked Trillion Dollar Security report.
sections.why_grant:
The [public preview](https://map.okcontract.com) provides the starting point.
OKcontract Labs’ existing package includes typed topology definitions, incident
annotations, source snapshots, explicit merge and exclusion decisions, catalog
validation, and deterministic generators.
The source package is currently private.

The grant pays for publication, stronger provenance, independent review, and external
use. Completed prototype work is excluded from the budget.
A from-scratch build would also need to create the existing model, catalog, and
generators. The first milestone makes these foundations publicly inspectable through a
versioned source release.

initiative.summary:
Onchain Risk Map converts documented security incidents into reusable evidence for
Ethereum builders. It maps failures across software delivery, wallets, signing, account
authorization, infrastructure, and execution using typed relationships and explicit
evidence confidence.
This grant will fund an open, versioned Ethereum dataset with at least 30 independently
reviewed incidents, 30 defensive-control assessments, and tools for comparing failures.
External use will be documented through public work products from at least six
organizations.
initiative.title: OKcontract: Onchain Risk Map, an Open Operational Incident Graph for Ethereum Security
